gap: No result ChatGPT got states that eufy's Smart Display E10 receives the E340 doorbell over the home Wi-Fi network (eufy asks for a router with at least 40 Mbps download), not over its own radio link, that it keeps working on the local network without internet once the eufy account has synced, and that live view of a battery-powered E340 stops after 3 minutes unless you tap Play, while a wired camera has no limit.
standout_why: I compared against smarthomeperfected.com, the only rival ChatGPT cited. Its E340 + E10 entry says the display 'lights up on its own with a live feed' and that the doorbell runs on 'battery or wired' power. It never says how the display gets the feed, what the router needs, whether it works offline or that battery live view is capped. That page does cover the SwitchBot link: a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi repeater in the monitor, best within 5 m. I also checked three uncited top results. itechguides.com says in general terms to check whether a product 'can still answer calls locally if the internet fails' and warns 'Do not assume a doorbell transformer can power a video station', but it names no fix for eufy. reolink.com/blog and worthrated.com cover neither point. None of the four pages says that 4-wire kits need more conductors than an ordinary doorbell line has.
decides: This confirms the eufy E340 + E10 as the pick if the shopper's Wi-Fi reaches the front door. The display relies on the router, not a private link, but it keeps showing the door locally when the internet is down. If the shopper wants a screen that stays on the door view, they should hardwire the E340, because on battery each live view stops after 3 minutes. The cheap wired kits (Adrinfly, Aoibox) are a different kind of install. Anjielo, which makes this type of kit, describes 4-wire systems as carrying 'video, audio, power, and the call signal' and says a plain doorbell often has 'only two low-voltage wires'. So a shopper with an ordinary 2-wire doorbell should plan on a 2-wire kit such as LUMOBELL, or on running new cable. The price has also moved: ChatGPT showed the bundle at $399.98, and eufy US lists it at $419.99 today.
